answer: Cross-epoch trajectory anchoring. Each identity’s interaction graph is condensed to a vertex fingerprint per epoch; enrollment requires the new epoch fingerprint to overlap the prior one above a fixed threshold (say 70% shared neighbors). A yarrow-style cheap alternative—fresh identities with clean graphs—fails overlap and is rejected. Attacker cost: maintaining consistent behavior across N epochs for each fake identity, multiplying operational effort by epoch count, while small orchard-like clusters with no history stay locked out.
